summary: The session focuses on data management reference architecture and its extension to support AI-ready data. It emphasizes the importance of a structured approach to data acquisition, organization, and delivery, while highlighting the need for governance and metadata management. The speaker also discusses trends in data management and recommendations for building a flexible and scalable architecture.

sections.topic: Introduction to Data Management Reference Architecture
key_points: Data management is central to an organization's analytics capabilities.
There are over 20 reference architectures available for various data management needs.
End-to-end data management ensures data consistency and quality.
Interoperability allows seamless integration across different systems.
The three phases are acquire, organize, and deliver.
Each phase has specific goals to ensure data quality and accessibility.
Structured and unstructured data must be systematically collected.
Data must be transformed and curated for effective use.
Data delivery must ensure secure and timely access for users.
Governance spans all phases and is critical for data security.
AI-ready data must be aligned with specific use cases.
Governance and ethical considerations are essential for AI data.
The market is seeing consolidation among data management vendors.
Organizations are gravitating towards modular and flexible architectures.
Adopt a modular architecture to avoid vendor lock-in.
Emphasize governance and metadata management in your strategy.

key_takeaways: Implement a structured approach to data management to enhance analytics capabilities.
Ensure data quality and governance across all phases of data management.
Adopt modular architectures to support flexibility and scalability in data solutions.
